learning_objectives.text: Raise a purchase order against an active supplier and submit it for approval
Complete the header fields correctly, distinguishing mandatory from optional
Explain what the budget check does and when it runs
Identify which approval level an order routes to from its value
Handle a blocked supplier, an absent approver and a failed transmission

excluded_assets.reason: The specification's own process-flow picture is redrawn as a diagram block on the same slide, so it stays legible at slide size and can be updated when the process changes. Content unchanged — see POFSD#2.

slides.title: Raising and Approving Purchase Orders

blocks.content: The Purchase Order module, end to end
Draft for trainer review · Written against Release R3

slides.speaker_notes: Set expectations: this session covers raising an order through to approval. It does not cover goods receipt or invoice matching.

slides.title: What you will be able to do

content: Raise a purchase order against an active supplier and submit it
Complete the header fields, knowing which are mandatory
Explain what the budget check does and when it runs
Identify which approval level an order routes to from its value
Handle a blocked supplier, an absent approver and a failed transmission

slides.speaker_notes: Read these out. Come back to them at the recap so people can check themselves against each one.

slides.title: How the session runs

content.title: Recap and where to get help

slides.speaker_notes: Two knowledge checks, one after creation and one after approval. Flag that now so nobody is surprised.

slides.title: An order moves through five states

blocks.content: Submitting an order runs a budget check. If it passes, the order goes to the approver. If it fails, it comes straight back to you.

diagram.caption: Purchase order states and the events that move an order between them.
diagram.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> Draft: Creator raises order
    Draft --> PendingApproval: Budget check passes
    Draft --> Draft: Budget check fails
    PendingApproval --> Approved: Approve
    PendingApproval --> Draft: Reject, comment required
    Approved --> Issued: Overnight transmission
    Draft --> Cancelled
    PendingApproval --> Cancelled
    Approved --> Cancelled
    Issued --> [*]

slides.speaker_notes: Walk the happy path first, then the two loops back to Draft. Most support calls are people who do not realise a failed budget check returns the order to Draft rather than holding it.

slides.title: What you can change in each state

blocks.content: An order is only editable in Draft. Once submitted, changes mean cancelling and raising a new order.

slides.speaker_notes: The Editable column is the one people need. Point out that Pending Approval is not editable even by the person who raised it.

slides.title: Three roles operate the module

blocks.content: Roles are assigned in the identity system, not in the PO module. If your role is wrong, that is a request to your manager, not a change you can make here.

rows: Create, edit and submit a draft order; cancel own draft
Approve or reject orders within their threshold; add comments
Edit the line items of an order under approval
Maintain supplier records; reopen an Issued order

slides.speaker_notes: The Cannot column matters most. Nobody approves their own order, and an approver who wants a line changed has to reject it back.

slides.title: The Create Purchase Order screen

content: Select the Supplier. Blocked suppliers do not appear in the list.
Set the Delivery Date. It must be today or later.
Check the Cost Centre — it defaults from your profile, and you can override it.
Add one line per item in the lines grid. Every order needs at least one line.
Save the draft, then Submit when you are ready for approval.

blocks.alt: The Create Purchase Order screen, showing the header fields above the lines grid.

blocks.content: Create Purchase Order — header above, lines grid below. Order Total is calculated and cannot be typed.

slides.speaker_notes: Have them follow along in the training system. The Order Total being read-only is the thing people try first and get stuck on.

slides.title: Header field rules

rows: Must be an active supplier; blocked suppliers are not selectable
Must be today or later; back-dating is rejected
Defaults from the requisitioner's profile; may be overridden

slides.speaker_notes: Three mandatory, two not. Internal Reference is the one teams use for their own tracking — worth a local convention.

slides.title: The budget check runs on submit, not on save

content: You can save a draft that would fail the budget check — saving does not test it
Submitting runs the check; passing sends the order to the approver
Failing returns the order to Draft and shows you the shortfall amount
A line quantity must be greater than zero
An order needs at least one line before it can be submitted

slides.speaker_notes: This catches people out: they save happily all afternoon, then submit and find the budget was never going to allow it.

slides.title: Creating an order

blocks.content: Five questions on what we have just covered.

questions.stem: You set a Delivery Date of yesterday and try to save. What happens?
options: The date is rejected — it must be today or later
The date is accepted but flagged for the approver
The date is silently reset to today
questions.rationale: Delivery Date is mandatory and must be today or later; back-dating is rejected outright.

questions.stem: A draft order can be saved even when there is not enough budget for it.
questions.rationale: True. The budget check runs on submit, not on save, so a draft that would fail can still be saved.

questions.stem: Which of these header fields can you leave empty?
options: Supplier
Internal Reference
Cost Centre
Delivery Date
questions.rationale: Internal Reference is the only optional field of the four; Supplier, Cost Centre and Delivery Date are all mandatory.

questions.stem: You can type the Order Total directly if the calculated figure looks wrong.
questions.rationale: False. Order Total is calculated from the lines and is read-only — correct the lines instead.

questions.stem: Your order fails the budget check on submit. Where does it go?
options: It stays in Pending Approval until budget is released
It returns to Draft and shows the shortfall amount
It routes to the Finance Director for an exception decision
questions.rationale: A failed budget check returns the order to Draft, and the requisitioner is shown the shortfall.

slides.speaker_notes: Give them two minutes, then take answers aloud. Q2 and Q5 are the pair that together explain the budget check.

slides.title: Approval level follows the order total

blocks.content: An order that exceeds your threshold routes to the next level. It is never split to keep it under a limit.

slides.speaker_notes: Watch the boundary: 5,000 exactly is Line Manager, 5,001 is Department Head.

slides.title: The Approve Purchase Order screen

blocks.content: Open the order from your approval queue.

content: Open the order from the approval queue.
Check the header, the lines and the budget check result.
Approve, or Reject with a comment of at least ten characters.
A rejected order returns to the creator as a Draft.

blocks.alt: The Approve Purchase Order screen, showing the approval queue and the budget check result.

blocks.content: Approve Purchase Order — the budget check result sits with the order header.

slides.speaker_notes: You cannot edit lines here. If a line is wrong, reject with a comment saying which line and why — that comment is all the creator gets.

slides.title: When something goes wrong

content: Approver absent — the order stays in their queue until a Procurement Admin reassigns it. There is no automatic escalation in R3.
Supplier blocked after the order was raised — approval is refused with 'Supplier is blocked'.
Transmission fails — the order stays Approved and appears on the overnight exception report.

slides.speaker_notes: The absent-approver case is the one that generates chasing emails. Tell them who their Procurement Admin is.

slides.title: Approving an order

blocks.content: Five questions on approval and exceptions.

questions.stem: An order totalling 48,000 is submitted. Who approves it?
options: Line Manager
Department Head
Finance Director
Line Manager, then Department Head
questions.rationale: 48,000 falls in the 5,001 to 50,000 band, which routes to the Department Head. Orders route to one level, not through several.

questions.stem: An order that exceeds your approval threshold can be split into two smaller orders to keep it within your limit.
questions.rationale: False. An order that exceeds a threshold routes to the next level; the specification states it is never split.

questions.stem: You want to approve an order but one line has the wrong quantity. What can you do on the approval screen?
options: Edit the line quantity, then approve
Approve with a comment noting the correction
Reject with a comment saying which line is wrong
questions.rationale: An approver cannot edit the line items of an order under approval. Rejecting with a comment sends it back to the creator as a Draft.

questions.stem: If an approver is on leave, the order sits in their queue until a Procurement Admin reassigns it.
questions.rationale: True. There is no automatic escalation in Release R3 — reassignment by a Procurement Admin is the only way the order moves.

questions.stem: An approved order fails to transmit to the supplier overnight. What is its status the next morning?
options: Approved, and listed on the overnight exception report
Issued, with a transmission warning
Returned to Draft for the creator to resubmit
questions.rationale: A failed transmission leaves the order in Approved and puts it on the overnight exception report; it does not reach Issued.

slides.speaker_notes: Q3 is the one approvers most often get wrong in practice — they expect to be able to fix a line rather than reject.

slides.title: An issued order commits budget

content: On reaching Issued, the order posts to the finance ledger as a commitment
Goods receipt is recorded in the warehouse system and matched back to the order line
Cancelling an order releases its commitment on the next ledger run

slides.speaker_notes: The delay on releasing a commitment is why cancelled orders can still show against budget for a day.

modules.title: Recap and where to get help

slides.title: The five things to take away

content: Supplier, Delivery Date and Cost Centre are mandatory; Order Total is calculated
The budget check runs on submit, not on save
A failed budget check returns the order to Draft with the shortfall shown
Approval level follows the order total, and an order is never split
An absent approver needs a Procurement Admin — nothing escalates on its own

slides.speaker_notes: Put the objectives slide back up beside this and ask whether anyone is unsure of one.

slides.title: Where to get help

blocks.gap_note: The specification does not name a support route, a service desk queue or a Procurement Admin contact. Needed before this deck is used, since two of the exception paths (absent approver, blocked supplier) end with 'contact a Procurement Admin' and nobody is told who that is. Leaves LO5 exposed.

slides.speaker_notes: Do not run this session without filling this in — the exceptions module sends people to a Procurement Admin we have not named.
